title: A Static for the Orbit
premise: Rafael Eriksen investigates impossible accidents aboard the relay ship Vesper Line, the only vessel licensed to travel between Earth's orbit and the silent colony Halcyon, whose founders fled a corporate war two generations ago. When Halcyon's children begin sharing an identical dream of a burning orbital, Rafael discovers the dream is a broadcast from cryosleep pods hidden in the colony's foundations — the frozen founders, half loyal to Earth, half to the rebellion, waking on a timer the colony's council buried. As the fleet truce expires, Rafael must choose which half of humanity to wake: the reconcilers who would surrender Halcyon's independence, or the hardliners who would burn the relay and sever the last link between worlds. In the end, Rafael wakes neither — instead broadcasting the founders' true, unedited last message to both worlds, letting the children who dreamed it decide, and the truce holds on the strength of that shared inheritance.
about_author: Ada Iversen is a former maritime insurance adjuster from Tromsø who turned to science fiction after a decade of investigating losses no one could explain. She writes on the night ferries between coastal towns, claiming the static between radio stations is where the best stories live.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Establishing the Vesper Line's eleven-day run between Earth orbit and silent Halcyon, and Rafael's reputation for solving 'impossible accidents' — losses with no cause an adjuster can name. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, a man at home only in transit.

chapters.title: Cargo That Dreams
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A routine claim: a Halcyon greenhouse failed, killing a crop worth a fleet pension. But the colony's children, playing nearby, all describe the same nightmare — a burning orbital. Rafael notes it in his ledger as coincidence. Beat: first unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Council archivist Maren Sol's POV. Maren keeps the colony's sealed founding records and notices Rafael pulling at threads. She warns him off with courtesy that reads as threat. Beat: the reader learns the council is hiding something about the founders.

chapters.title: Impossible Accident Number Nine
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael reconstructs the greenhouse failure and finds it wasn't failure at all — the environmental systems were deliberately rerouted to power something beneath the colony, something drawing megawatts in its sleep. Beat: the investigator realizes the accident is a symptom.

chapters.title: The Children's Chorus
chapters.summary: Ten-year-old Ivo Sol's POV, Maren's nephew. Ivo describes the dream from inside it: the burning orbital, a woman's voice counting down. The children have started meeting secretly to compare details. Beat: wonder curdling into fear; the dream is getting more precise.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with Maren. Maren, guilt-stricken, shows Rafael the sealed level: two hundred cryopods in two locked banks, one keyed to Earth's codes, one to the rebellion's. The founders froze their own schism instead of resolving it. Beat: revelation reframes everything — Halcyon is a held breath.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Captain Okonkwo's POV, transmitting from the blockade line. The forty-year truce expires in ninety days; after that, Earth reclaims Halcyon by force unless the colony acknowledges the succession pact. Beat: a clock starts ticking over every scene to come.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The council splits: wake the reconciler pods and negotiate, or the hardliner pods and fight. Rafael, as neutral investigator, is proposed — to his horror — as the tiebreaker. Beat: a man whose job is assigning blame is handed the power to decide a war.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Dream
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The children decode the dream's countdown: it matches the truce expiry to the day. The voice belongs to Founder Ines Halvorsen, and the dream isn't a malfunction — it's a message, sent pod-to-pod through the colony's power grid. Beat: children realize adults have been lying to them.

chapters.title: Accident, or Assassination
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A saboteur tries to destroy the reconciler pod bank and make it look like another impossible accident. Rafael catches the reroute signature — the same hand behind the greenhouse. Someone wants only one half to wake. Beat: paranoia; the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She admits her father helped bury the succession pact and that the council has been siphoning pod power for forty years, slowly killing the sleepers to keep the secret cold. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh — Maren chooses truth at the cost of her family's name.

chapters.title: The Blockade Tightens
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Earth's fleet moves up its timetable after intercepting Halcyon's encrypted traffic. Okonkwo privately doubts the war is just but follows orders; she requests Rafael's investigation files. Beat: the antagonist revealed as a mirror of Rafael — another loyal servant of a system she doubts.

chapters.title: Static on the Line
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael smuggles evidence toward Earth via the relay, but the transmission is jammed by someone on the Vesper Line itself — his own crew is compromised. Beat: betrayal; the neutral route between worlds was never neutral.

chapters.title: Ivo Runs the Corridors
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The children, knowing the adults will stall, physically occupy the pod vault to prevent the hardliner bank from being force-woken early. Ivo leads them using dream-knowledge of the vault's layout. Beat: children act where adults freeze; courage without fully understanding stakes.

chapters.title: The Founder's Testimony
chapters.summary: Rafael and Maren's alternating POV. They wake Ines Halvorsen alone — a controlled, partial revival — and she tells the truth the pods were frozen to hide: the schism was manufactured by Earth's corporations to fracture the colony, and the pods were her insurance, not her weapon. Beat: the inheritance is a lie inherited.

chapters.title: Impossible Accident Number Ten
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The saboteur, exposed as the council's own security chief, vents the vault. Rafael saves Ivo but the reconciler bank is half-destroyed — the choice is collapsing toward waking the hardliners by default. Beat: darkest moment; Rafael's ledger of accidents finally has a name on every page, and it's his side's.

chapters.title: What Rafael Investigates Last
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, intimate and reflective. Facing the truce deadline with a broken choice, Rafael re-reads his own case files and realizes every 'impossible accident' was the colony's buried conscience leaking — the pods dreaming through the grid, trying to be found. Beat: his identity as blame-assigner dissolves; he was never investigating accidents, only an unspoken plea.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rafael, Maren, and Ivo's braided POV. Instead of waking either bank, they patch Ines's unedited testimony into the relay and broadcast it in the clear to both the fleet and the colony — the children's dream, made public, undeniable. Beat: climax; truth as the only move that beats both loyalty and force.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Choice
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The fleet demands she fire on the relay. Confronted with proof the war was manufactured, she stalls, then refuses the order, buying the colony its deadline. Beat: the antagonist's mirror completes — she makes the same choice Rafael did, loyalty bending to truth.

chapters.title: Counting Down Together
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Truce expiry day. The children, who shared the dream, now share the vigil; both pod banks are opened to the colonists' democratic vote, and the colony votes — narrowly — to wake both halves together, reconcilers and hardliners, and let them argue in the open. Beat: the inheritance is finally claimed rather than buried.

chapters.title: A Static for the Orbit
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The founders wake into a colony that already knows their worst secrets and chose them anyway. Rafael signs his last report: cause of all accidents, 'unresolved grief, now resolved.' He takes the Vesper Line out one more time, both worlds speaking on the open channel. Beat: release; the man of transit finally has somewhere to arrive.

chapters.title: The Next Route
chapters.summary: Ivo and Maren's closing POV, years later. Ivo, now a relay apprentice, dreams no more of fire — but sometimes, on quiet nights, the whole orbit shares a small, good dream: a ship on the long route, carrying mail between worlds that talk. Beat: resolution and inheritance passed forward; identity rebuilt on connection instead of silence.
